title: Clear-Down of the Qualifying Count at the Close of a Wanderlane Traveller Club Period
content:
The qualifying count on a Wanderlane Traveller Club statement does not run on from one period into the next, and this note explains what the statement shows when a period closes.

**The clear-down itself.** At the close of a qualifying period the whole qualifying count is cleared down to nothing in one movement, and the next period begins on the day the reviewed tier takes effect.

**What it does not touch.** The clear-down never touches the spendable balance, and a member who has just been promoted starts the new period at zero rather than carrying a surplus forward.

**A period that closes before the decision.** Where a review is still undecided when the period closes, the count is held rather than cleared, and the clear-down follows the decision.

**A membership in grace.** A membership in grace after a failed review keeps accruing into the new period, and the accruals stand whether or not the tier eventually drops.

**Corrections and appeals.** A correction to an earlier qualifying accrual is posted against the period it belonged to, not the period it is discovered in. A clear-down is never reversed; a count restored after an appeal is restored by a fresh qualifying accrual carrying the appeal's reference.

## The statement read at the close of a period

| What the record shows at the close | What happens to the qualifying count |
| --- | --- |
| The review is decided | The whole count is cleared down to nothing in one movement, and the next period begins on the day the reviewed tier takes effect |
| The review is still undecided | The count is held rather than cleared, and the clear-down follows the decision |
| The member has just been promoted | The new period opens at zero, with no surplus carried forward |
| The member is in grace after a failed review | Accrual continues into the new period, and those accruals stand whether or not the tier eventually drops |

## Points of judgement

*A qualifying accrual that belonged to a period now closed is found to be wrong.* The correction is posted against the period it belonged to, not the period it is discovered in.

*An appeal succeeds and the member asks for their cleared count back.* The clear-down is not reversed. The count is restored by a fresh qualifying accrual carrying the appeal's reference.

*A member asks whether the clear-down costs them their spendable points.* It does not. The clear-down never touches the spendable balance; the two counts on the card are separate.
